lines.author: ai
lines.content: A Utility Line Assignment (ULA) is a City of Edmonton requirement for installing utility assets within the road allowance where ground disturbance is required. The ULA application covers new installations, modifications, or maintenance of aerial and underground facilities in that road allowance where ground disturbance is required. The City circulates each application to stakeholders, advises the designer of any conflicts or objections, and approves the application and proposed facility locations.

lines.author: ai
lines.content: Processing of a Utility Line Assignment (ULA) application involves several steps by the City of Edmonton. The City of Edmonton Transportation Office acknowledges receipt of an online ULA application, provides the name of a contact person and the time frame of the process, and circulates the proposed design to all stakeholders. A stakeholder may respond to the circulation with conflicts, and the City advises the designer of those conflicts or objections. In step 9.0 of the ULA process, the City approves the application and issues a ULA permit number.

lines.author: ai
lines.content: The City of Edmonton's ULA application administrator circulates applications only to ATCO Pipelines, so other pipeline companies are not aware of a project unless the designer applies to them directly for a high pressure pipeline crossing and/or a proximity agreement. A high pressure pipeline crossing requires a direct application to the pipeline company. A proximity agreement is an agreement applied for directly to a pipeline company when a project is near that company's facilities.
